answer: Operator collateral cross-default: each agent identity is cryptographically tied to an operator's shared collateral pool. If any identity on a knoll of linked identities is caught sybil-farming, the whole pool is slashed and the operator's other identities are frozen. An attacker must therefore risk a hollow reserve large enough to cover every identity they run, not just one. Duplicating identities multiplies exposure across the meadow of accounts, so each new identity raises the operator's total at-risk capital linearly.
